reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that helping the Hebrew people is a goal of Yahweh. In 1 Samuel 9:16, God tells Samuel He will send a man to anoint as prince over Israel 'and he shall save my people from the hand of the Philistines: for I have looked upon my people, because their cry is come unto me.' Additionally, in 1 Samuel 10:18-19, Samuel reminds the people that Yahweh previously brought them out of Egypt and delivered them from their oppressors. The narrative establishes both God's historical acts of deliverance on behalf of Israel and His expressed present intention to continue helping them by selecting Saul as their deliverer. The Hebrew terms וְהוֹשִׁיעַ (to save/deliver) and צַעֲקָת֖וֹ אֵלָֽי (their cry came to me) indicate active divine concern and purposeful intervention on behalf of the people.
